we have upgraded the Level-2 trigger to provide the same MET resolution as the Level-1 trigger.
the Level-2 MET resolution is improved by a factor of 1.5 and that the Level-1 MET resolution is improved from 1.0 to 0.8, with the corresponding improvement in the trigger efficiency.

the following points: 1. the design of a Level-2 trigger algorithm to improve the resolution of the missing transverse energy (MET) and SUMET calculations, and the implementation in the Pulsar VME board; 2. the design of an improved Level-1 calorimetry system based on the PULSAR board, and its implementation in the Level-1 trigger system.
the development of the trigger system of a large particle physics detector, and with the development of new trigger algorithms for the search of rare physics processes.
the design of the trigger algorithms for the CDF experiment at Fermilab.

the new CDF Level-1 and the upgraded Level-3 calorimeters are the most advanced trigger system ever built for a high energy collider experiment.
the CDF Level 3 calorimeter upgrade has been a success.

the CDF calorimeter upgrade is a very successful example of a fast and flexible trigger system, able to cope with the increasing luminosity and to provide a very high quality of the trigger samples.

the CDF Level 2 and Level 1 calorimeter upgrades have been successfully implemented, and that the Level 2 calorimeter trigger system is now fully operational at the CDF experiment.
